THE OPERATING CONTEXT

Equipment condition monitoring

An operations team needs to understand changing equipment conditions across a facility without checking every asset manually.

  1. 01Capture a selected sensor reading
  2. 02Normalize the device and timestamp
  3. 03Review trends in an operational dashboard
  4. 04Route a threshold exception to the responsible team
DESIGNED OUTCOME

An agreed view of asset conditions, an exception history, and a clear follow-up process. The pilot validates connectivity and useful signals before a wider rollout.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS

Decisions that
shape delivery.

01Devices & protocols
Review the existing hardware, available interfaces, gateway needs, and communication methods. Device compatibility is established before the platform architecture is committed.
02Data & connectivity
Agree sampling frequency, time handling, retention, buffering, and behavior during interrupted connections. Capture the information the operation needs at a sustainable cost.
03Access & operations
Define device identity, user roles, monitoring, update ownership, and alert escalation. The operating model is considered alongside the dashboard.
A USEFUL STARTING BRIEF

Bring the context.
We’ll shape the next step.

  • Equipment or asset list

  • Network and site constraints
  • A practical pilot location

QUESTIONS & ANSWERS

Before your iot platforms & connectivity project.

Clear answers help define the right next step. Your project scope and responsibilities are agreed before delivery.

Ask the team

We start by reviewing the available interfaces, protocols, permissions, and network conditions. Some assets may need a gateway or additional sensing; the assessment establishes what can be connected.

A replacement is not assumed. We assess the existing devices and identify where reuse, adapters, or additional hardware make sense for the agreed monitoring objective.

Buffering, retry behavior, recovery, and connectivity alerts are defined around the selected devices and operational needs. The pilot should test the relevant interruption scenarios.

Monitoring and control are different scopes. Any equipment-control functionality requires an explicit design, permitted interfaces, operating boundaries, and appropriate validation.

Yes. A focused pilot can validate device connectivity, data quality, dashboard usefulness, and the follow-up workflow before deciding how to expand.

The agreed handover can include architecture, device mappings, platform access, alert rules, operational guidance, and support responsibilities. Hardware installation and maintenance ownership are defined in the engagement.
